content.title: Iowa City business owner purchases former SpareMe bowling property
content.text: IOWA CITY, Iowa (KCRG) - A new business plans to take over the former SpareMe Bowl & Arcade space at the Chauncey building in Iowa City. Local business owner Joe Hill purchased the property and plans to reopen the space as Barker’s Bowling this summer, according to the Iowa City Downtown District. Hill also owns Burger Haul in the Pedestrian Mall. Hill says there will be two floors of bowling with 12 lanes total. There are also plans for pool tables, shuffleboard courts and a dance floor for live entertainment. In addition, both floors will have full bar service, and offer diner foods such as pizza, burgers, ice cream and shakes. The second floor will double as a rentable event venue space for birthdays, corporate events or other gatherings. Hill says the business will bring back the unique gathering space that helped shape downtown Iowa City’s identity. “I look at this as a real opportunity,” Hill said in a statement. “When this space closed, it left a void in downtown. This is about bringing something back that enhances the district and extends what downtown has to offer. It’s an entertainment venue that gives everyone a place to go, whether you visit after a movie with FilmScene next door, after the Farmers Market on Saturdays, or a night out with friends. I want people to come in, enjoy the atmosphere, the food, the entertainment, and leave already thinking about their next visit.”SpareMe Bowl & Arcade, alongside the Chauncey Hotel and hotelVetro — all owned by Hawkeye Hotels — closed in November of 2025 after the properties failed to sell at auction.Hill said community is the focus of the space. “Barker’s is meant to be a place for everyone,” he said. “Whether you’re coming with family, meeting friends, or just looking for something fun to do, it’s a space where you can step away from the day-to-day and enjoy yourself. Bowling is something simple, but it brings people together, and that’s what this is all about.”Christopher Hunter, Director of Marketing & Communications at the Iowa City Downtown District, said having the space open for bowling again is a win for locals.“Downtown thrives when we have destinations like this that bring people together, create energy throughout the day and night, and serve as an anchor for community life,” Hunter said in a statement. “It’s exactly the kind of investment that strengthens the vitality of our urban core.”The Downtown District says construction is currently underway and a grand opening will be announced in the coming months.
